chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

He asked him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was listening: 'What is the limit of the illness due to which the fasting is left?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he is not able to have the pre-dawn meal (suhoor).'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific medical limit that exempts a Muslim from fasting during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a practical, objective legal criterion (mudda) for the exemption from fasting, linking the severity of illness to the physical capacity to perform suhoor. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that the burden of fasting is lifted not merely by the presence of disease, but when it impedes the fundamental act of pre-dawn nourishment, reflecting the principle of 'la haraj' (no hardship).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Bakr Bin Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said,

‘My father asked him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I was listening, ‘What is the limit of the illness due to which the Fasting can be left?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he is not able upon having the pre-dawn meal’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Bakr ibn abu Bakr al-Hadramiy who has said the following: “

Once my father asked him (abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam ) and I was listening, ‘What is the limit of an illness because of which it is permissible to stop fasting?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is when one is not able to take Suhur (breakfast in the morning before dawn).”’
